extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers seeking an encyclopedic summary of the Bill Cosby criminal trial
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic article summarizing the procedural history, motions, evidentiary rulings, trials, verdicts, appeals, and legal standards in a single high-profile criminal case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of other-accuser testimony (prior bad acts / pattern evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution may move to introduce testimony from other alleged victims to show a 'method of operation' or pattern of conduct; the trial court decides how many and which such witnesses are admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts balance similarity/remoteness and probative value against prejudice; the Superior Court upheld admission of five of nineteen witnesses as suggesting a 'distinct, signature pattern' in Cosby's conduct. Remoteness in time and dissimilarity to charged acts are common grounds to exclude such evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of recorded conversations based on recording-law jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorded calls may be admissible if law of the place of recording permits them (e.g., Canada allows one-party consent), affecting admissibility in U.S. trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional consent rules (one-party vs two-party consent) determine whether recordings can be introduced; courts will consider where and how the recording was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior civil deposition testimony in criminal trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony or depositions from related civil litigation can be admitted into criminal proceedings (e.g., Cosby's 2005 deposition was allowed into the criminal trial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to seal or re-seal such depositions may be denied; admission can include admissions of past behavior (e.g., statements about Quaaludes). Challenges on appeal may argue such use renders a trial unfair or requires suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of irrelevant or unduly prejudicial evidence (relevance vs prejudice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts exclude material that is insufficiently relevant or that would be unduly prejudicial (e.g., the judge excluded Cosby's book references to 'Spanish Fly' but allowed testimony about Quaaludes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges apply rules weighing probative value against potential for unfair prejudice; specific items (books, past statements) may be admitted or excluded accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of venue and jury selection to mitigate pretrial publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants may seek change of venue or jurors drawn from outside the local pool when local media coverage could taint jurors; courts may permit an out-of-county jury while keeping trial location unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may order jury pool from another county (Allegheny County was used here), permit questionnaires, limit number of jurors summoned, and control selection procedures to reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juror sequestration and screening procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts can sequester juries and employ screening measures during selection to protect impartiality (the judge ordered a sequestered jury in this case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense and prosecution may propose questionnaires, large pools of potential jurors, or extra peremptory strikes; the judge controls scope and may deny extraordinary requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury unanimity requirement and mistrial for deadlock
rubrics_metrics.description: A deadlocked jury unable to reach a unanimous verdict can result in a mistrial (Judge O'Neill declared a mistrial after the jury was 'hopelessly deadlocked').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported split votes and shifting juror positions can cause deadlock; prosecution may seek retrial after mistrial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations as a limit on criminal prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Many alleged acts may fall outside criminal statutes of limitations, preventing prosecution for older allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute of limitations varies by offense and jurisdiction; only timely allegations can typically form the basis of criminal charges unless exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecutorial statements/promises not to prosecute and due-process reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A prosecutor's public statement or promise not to prosecute can create an expectation on which a defendant may rely; the Pennsylvania Supreme Court found an unwritten promise by a prior DA prevented later prosecution in Cosby's case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defendant relied on a non-prosecution statement (e.g., by testifying in civil litigation), courts may find 5th and 14th Amendment violations and bar prosecution or suppress evidence; remedies can range from suppression to overturning convictions depending on remedy deemed appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probative vs prejudicial balancing (appellate review ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission of evidence is reviewed under the standard of whether testimony or evidence is more probative than prejudicial; appeals can argue evidence was unduly prejudicial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate courts examine whether trial courts properly balanced relevance and prejudice, and whether admission affected a fair trial; disagreements on this balance are common appellate issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretrial motions to dismiss based on due process, prosecutorial misconduct, or statute of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants may file motions to dismiss alleging due-process violations, prosecutorial misconduct, or that the statute of limitations has expired; trial courts rule on these motions pretrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions can be denied (as occurred several times here) and such denials are often the basis for appeals; courts assess factual and legal sufficiency of the claims when ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bail determination and assessment of flight risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Bail is set based on considerations including flight risk; Cosby's bail was set at $1 million with surrender of passport as conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations (e.g., ownership of a private plane) may influence prosecutors' requests to revoke bail or increase conditions; judges evaluate risk of flight and community safety when setting bail.
